business_scope.primary_industry_name: Commercial Soundscape Licensing and Audio Sample Subscriptions

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008 (as amended), sections 11 (name reservations), 13 (incorporation), 14 (notice of incorporation), 15 (Memorandum of Incorporation), 19 (legal personality), and 66 (board of directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), Department of Trade, Industry and Competition
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) accompanied by the Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement. A private company may issue one or more shares of any par value; no escrow account or capital deposit is required for incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the company is incorporated and the Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation filed with CIPC are approved. RESOLVED FURTHER that the provisional director and members accept office, and the registered office be and is hereby fixed at the business address recorded on the Notice of Incorporation. RESOLVED FURTHER that the subscriber share allotment be accepted in accordance with the MOI, and that [Name] and [Name] be and are hereby appointed as directors, subject to the Companies Act 71 of 2008. RESOLVED FURTHER that the first auditor and company secretary, if required, are appointed, and the directors are authorised to open bank accounts, execute SARS registrations, and cause the certificate of incorporation to be issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit Form CoR 9.1 via the CIPC e-Services portal. Pay the name reservation fee and ensure the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and does not violate section 11 of the Companies Act. The reservation remains valid for six calendar months.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 9.1 (Application for Reservation of Name)
Certified copy of the incorporator's identity document or passport
Proof of name reservation fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file an objection or apply for a fresh alternative name via CIPC within 20 business days; alternatively, proceed with a randomly generated CIPC registration number and adopt a secondary name at a later point.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare the Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC registrations desk, or legal advisor / CIPC standard template system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) using CIPC's standard template, specifying the company's private status, number of directors, share structure, and registered office. Execute the Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) and MOI before a commissioner of oaths. Each incorporator must sign, and witness signatures are required where applicable.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 15.1)
Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1)
Consent letter from each incorporator
Consent to act as director forms (CoR 14.1 Annexure)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC queries the MOI provisions, amend the non-complying clauses to align with the Companies Act and Schedule 2 standard provisions, and resubmit within the CIPC deadline (usually 10 business days from the notice of query).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the incorporation application to CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into CIPC e-Services and select 'Register a new company'. Upload the completed CoR 14.1 and signed MOI, pay the statutory incorporation fee electronically, and submit. CIPC will verify the application, issue a corporate registration number, and generate an electronic Certificate of Incorporation once approved.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1)
Signed Memorandum of Incorporation
Proof of online payment of incorporation fee
Notarised power of attorney, if filing through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected, correct the specified deficiencies and re-file within 30 days; minor corrections after payment are accepted without an additional filing fee, but a fresh fee applies if a new incorporation number is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company for tax and statutory obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling portal; also the Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) and Compensation Fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the CIPC Certificate of Incorporation to register as a taxpayer on SARS eFiling. Obtain an income tax reference number, register for UIF and Skills Development Levy as an employer, and apply for VAT registration if expected annual taxable turnover exceeds ZAR 1 million. Register under the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act (COIDA) if employees will be engaged.
required_dossiers: CIPC electronic Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum of Incorporation
Certified copies of directors' identity documents
Proof of registered office address (e.g., lease agreement or utility bill)
Bank account details once opened
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS does not finalise registration within the service standard, submit a follow-up via the SARS eFiling ticketing system with certified supporting documents, and request a manual verification appointment at a SARS branch if further authentication is needed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a corporate bank account and activate payment rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banking institution in South Africa (e.g., FNB, Standard Bank, ABSA, or Nedbank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the incorporation certificate, MOI, directors' identities, and SARS tax reference number to the chosen bank. Complete the bank's know-your-client (KYC) and Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA) forms. Once the account is active, connect Stripe and PayPal using the corporate bank account and the registered legal entity name 'ZA PTY LTD'.
required_dossiers: CIPC Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum of Incorporation
SARS tax registration number confirmation
Directors' certified identity or passport copies
Proof of residential and business address for FICA
Bank account questionnaire and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the account opening is delayed, provide an updated board resolution confirming the signatories and their ownership percentages. If FICA documentation is incomplete, obtain a notarised resolution and resubmit the full package to the bank's compliance team.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no physical manufacturing or industrial plant is operated. If a recording studio or office is occupied, the local municipal zoning and building control authority may have jurisdiction.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable for a purely digital audio-licensing marketplace; a standard municipal business/trading licence may be required at the registered office, depending on municipal by-laws.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environmental Affairs (DEA) – Environmental Impact Assessment Directorate
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the activity of commercial soundscape licensing and audio sample subscriptions is not listed in the EIA Regulations Listing Notices 1, 2 or 3. A Basic Assessment will only be triggered if a physical recording studio with construction works or high-noise operations is established.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for digital operations. If a physical studio is established, noise levels must comply with SANS 10103 'The measurement and rating of environmental noise' and local municipal noise by-laws; no volatile organic compound or effluent discharge is associated with this activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For leased office premises, obtain a fire safety certificate from the local Fire Protection Services, an electrical compliance certificate, and ensure compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 regarding first aid, welfare facilities, and COIDA registration for any employees. No structural load inspections are required beyond the landlord's building clearance for ordinary office or studio use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) – eFiling portal at www.sars.gov.za / www.efiling.gov.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Incorporation with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) triggers automatic provisional SARS income tax registration linked to the company registration number. Final statutory registration must be completed via SARS eFiling by submitting IRP12/ING forms (income tax) and VAT101 (VAT) within 21 days of incorporation or before commencing business. Foreign-owned (Pty) Ltd entities are treated no differently from domestic private companies; non-resident ownership is permitted. Physical verification documents, bank confirmation, and the signed MoI may be requested.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or free-floating entity classification election. A South African private company is per se a separate tax resident subject to entity-level corporate income tax (currently 27%). Available statutory elections include: VAT grouping election under section 50 of the VAT Act (for qualifying group companies), section 12E micro-business turnover tax election for small qualifying companies (annual turnover ≤ ZAR 1 million), functional currency election under section 25D for businesses with cash flows substantially in a foreign currency, and the section 80A–80M hybrid mismatch provisions apply automatically to hybrid entities/instruments, not by election. Certain CFC and limited-interest relief elections may apply to cross-border structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991 as amended)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration: taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 per annum (12-month period). Voluntary registration: taxable supplies at least ZAR 50,000 per annum. For foreign suppliers of electronic services to South African residents, a separate ZAR 50,000 mandatory registration threshold applies (s.23 VAT Act).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping regime is currently mandatory for domestic businesses. E-invoicing is optional but SARS has adopted PEPPOL standards to facilitate interoperable tax invoices. Where applicable, a full tax invoice under s.20(4) VAT Act must be issued within 21 days of supply and must contain the specified particulars (known seller, VAT number, invoice date, description, VAT-exclusive/inclusive amounts). VAT returns and invoice integrity checks are submitted through the SARS eFiling API; auditable records for at least 5 years are required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods is zero-rated if the goods are physically exported from South Africa and documentary proof of export is retained (s.11(1)(a) VAT Act). Export of services is zero-rated under s.11(2)(k) where the recipient is a non-resident who is outside South Africa at the time performance is rendered, the services are not in respect of anything physically in South Africa, and neither the services nor the intellectual property are used or possessed in South Africa. For a royalty-free stock music licensing subscription, the digital/electronic licence supplied to a non-resident customer is typically zero-rated provided the customer is not in South Africa, the licence fee is paid from outside the common customs area, and the music is not acquired for use/exploitation in South Africa. Where the recipient is a South African resident or the music is consumed in South Africa, the supply is subject to 15% VAT as an electronic service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading / Airwaybill / Electronic Proof of Export
Inward Remittance Certificate (foreign currency payment proof)
Signed licensing agreement / music licence sale contract
VAT tax invoice or commercial invoice in the required form
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS will deny zero-rating if the export or consumption conditions are not supported by contemporaneous documentary proof retained for at least 5 years. Where zero-rated invoices are found not to have been genuinely exported (e.g., electronic licence accessed or consumed in South Africa, or export documentation is fabricated), SARS retrospectively claws back the unpaid 15% VAT together with interest. Under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011, understatement penalties of up to 200% of the tax shortfall may be imposed for intentional disregard or gross negligence, and criminal prosecution for tax evasion carries imprisonment and/or monetary sanctions. SARS also imposes a 10% late-payment penalty plus statutory interest for VAT due arising from clawback assessments.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through its Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) as the exchange-control authority under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act 9 of 1933), together with the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) for AML/CFT supervision; operational execution is delegated to Authorized Dealers (licensed South African commercial banks).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African Rand (ZAR) is a floating currency with a managed convertible regime. Current-account transactions - royalty income, digital audio-licensing fees and subscription receipts from foreign customers - are convertible and repatriable without prior SARB approval, subject to Authorized Dealer documentation and SARS Tax Compliance Status verification. Capital-account transactions are regulated: inward foreign direct investment in the form of equity subscriptions is freely permitted and only requires BOP reporting by the Authorized Dealer, while outbound resident capital flows, resident exposure to offshore NDF markets and certain intercompany loans require FinSurv approval. Profit-remittance hurdles consist primarily of tax gates rather than exchange control: dividends to non-resident shareholders attract South African dividends tax at the statutory rate of 20% (treaty relief available) and royalties paid to non-residents attract a 15% withholding tax under section 49B of the Income Tax Act; a SARS tax-clearance certificate is always required before a cross-border dividend remittance is processed by the bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Exchange Control Regulation 6 and the SARB Exchange Control Manual, all export proceeds - expressly including royalties, license fees and electronic-service receipts for ISIC 5920 audio licensing - must be received in the Republic of South Africa within 180 days of the invoice date or the date the service is rendered. Repatriated foreign currency must be surrendered by conversion into ZAR through the company's Authorized Dealer at the prevailing market rate, giving a mandatory conversion ratio of 100% for all repatriated proceeds, unless the company holds a SARB-approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) in which qualifying export proceeds may be retained unconverted. No general permission exists for a South African resident to hold export income offshore beyond the 180-day window; retention in an overseas platform wallet (Stripe or PayPal) beyond that period without a documented Authorized Dealer arrangement constitutes a contravention. De minimis transaction and documentary exemptions follow the SARB General Authorizations; non-compliance attracts statutory penalties, interest and escalation of the entity's compliance risk rating with its lending bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (annual statement confirming incorporation particulars, directors, shareholding and beneficial ownership)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 30 business days after each anniversary of incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts escalating CIPC penalties (approx. ZAR 200–300 per submission); continued non-filing after compliance notification may lead to administrative strike-off, dissolution of the company, and disqualification of directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (UBO) register filing and annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: UBO register must be filed annually with the annual return; changes in beneficial ownership reported within 7 business days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or non-filing is an offence under the Companies Act; CIPC may issue a compliance notice, impose administrative fines, and record a contravention against the company.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the Public Interest Score (PI score) is 350 or more, or if the company is required to prepare audited financial statements under a regulatory licence or contract. Below 350, compilation under the Close Corporations / Independent Review regime applies; PI score 100–349 requires an independent review, below 100 allows self-review if no other trigger.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for the South African context (IFRS or IFRS for SMEs) adopted under Companies Act 71 of 2008 and the Financial Reporting Standards Framework

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register and confirm its contents with the CIPC as part of every annual return. Shareholding transfers require simultaneous amendment of the company's securities register and UBO register within 7 business days, with no exemption for private (Pty) companies.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 80 – 150 per annum for CIPC registered office and agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 – 4,500 per annum for an independent review or audit, depending on company complexity and PI score

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Company Income Tax Return) filed via SARS eFiling (www.sarsefiling.co.za); provisional tax via IRP6
stage_6.reporting_frequency: Annually; provisional tax payments (IRP6) are due bi-annually (first payment within 6 months of the start of the year of assessment; second payment on the last day of the year of assessment)
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: The ITR14 must be filed within 12 months after the end of the company's financial year (the company's 'year of assessment'); e.g., a 31 December 2025 FYE return is due by 31 December 2026

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SARS tax reference number, registered name, registered address, financial year-end, and category of taxpayer
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the SA-registered entity's details; non-resident shareholders are not reflected on the ITR14 (their identity is declared via the dividends tax declaration)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income including audio library licensing subscriptions, one-off royalty-free licence downloads, and ancillary sync fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A resident (Pty) Ltd reports worldwide income; foreign sourced income may qualify for exemption under s9 if effectively foreign-source

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions: cost of recorded master assets amortised under s11(gC), royalties and revenue-share paid to musicians, platform fees (Stripe/PayPal), hosting, marketing, and salaries
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct expenses actually incurred in the production of income (s11(a)); payments to non-resident artists attract 15% royalty withholding tax (s49B) unless treaty reduced

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance of assessed loss brought forward from prior years
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Assessed losses are carried forward indefinitely but are set off against taxable income of only 80% per year (s20 ITA)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by 27% headline rate; includes calculation of dividends tax credits (CGT included via taxable capital gains at 80% inclusion rate)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Capital gains of companies are included at 80% effective inclusion; CGT from disposal of shares in the (Pty) Ltd is reported by the non-resident in their own jurisdiction

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section I – Provisional tax and prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IRP6 provisional tax payments already made (first and second provisional) credited against the assessed liability
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Companies must pay provisional tax even if the expected liability is below the threshold; under-estimation attracts penalties under s163(1) TAA
